notes:
I wasn't able to write any notes on Psalm 30 this time.

I sent requests for six pages at once: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub, the NET Bible notes, and Precept Austin. My code crashed before it could read the replies because I handled the returned data wrongly, and I then hit the limit on tool calls for this turn. I never read a single word from any of those pages.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have no page content, I have nothing I can honestly give you with a URL. Writing "v. 1: … v. 12: …" notes now would mean making them up, so I've left them out.

**What I'd do on the next attempt (just ask me to continue):**
1. **Main readings:** read those same six pages again, verse by verse, plus StudyLight (for Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* and others) and Blue Letter Bible.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** check whether the teachers actually disagree on:
   - v. 1, the heading "dedication of the temple" (which building, and whether it's David's own experience or a later use).
   - vv. 2–3, whether "healed" means a real illness and whether "Sheol"/"the Pit" means near-death or something more.
   - v. 5, God's anger and favour in the believer's life.
   - vv. 6–7, overconfidence in good times and God hiding his face (relevant to how traditions teach assurance).
   - v. 9, what the Old Testament thought about praise after death.

   For each tradition I'd use its own teachers (Ligonier and TGC; Spurgeon and Desiring God; Wesley's notes; LCMS and 1517; Enduring Word and Sam Storms).
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship; New Advent (the Church Fathers on Psalm 29/30, since older Catholic Bibles number the Psalms differently) and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'd check v. 5 and vv. 11–12 for prosperity or word-of-faith uses, and only include them if the sites actually discuss them.
